zones.what: Deck 6 balcony cabins sit directly at lifeboat/davit level, and the obstruction tapers off but is still detectable looking down at roughly a 45-degree angle from decks 7, 8 and 9 above.
zones.effect: On Deck 6 the boats and davits block a straight-down view of the water; on 7-9 the horizon/outward view stays clear but a steep downward glance still catches boat structure. Cruise Solstice's own deck-by-deck notes pinpoint the worst stretch as the cabins fronting the largest boats.
zones.mattersTo: Photographers and anyone who wants to watch the water directly below (dolphins, embarkation activity) will be disappointed on Deck 6; guests who mainly want an open horizon/sunset view are largely unaffected, especially on 7-9.
zones.source: cruisecritic.com editor review + cruisemapper.com cabin page + cruisedeckplans.com deck-6 notes + first-person Cruise Critic review 93364
zones.leadDetail: See leads for named cabin ranges (6155-6178, 6187-6206).

zones.what: Portside forward cabins on Deck 3 sit directly beneath the nightclub venue one deck up (Deck 4), and accessible cabins on this deck are described as right forward, near the theatre and just forward of the nightclub/Celebrity Central above.
zones.effect: Bass and late-night nightclub activity can be heard through the floor in this specific forward stretch; starboard-side cabins under the casino/entertainment court by contrast draw little complaint.
zones.mattersTo: Light sleepers and anyone doing an early port day should avoid the named portside-forward range; night owls who are out late anyway won't notice.
zones.source: cruisedeckplans.com Deck 3 notes + Cruise Critic boards thread on Deck 3 accessible cabins

zones.what: Deck 3 cabins sit at the level of the ship's 3-deck Grand Foyer atrium, which hosts live music, auctions and daily events.
zones.effect: Cruisers repeatedly report hearing music and crowd noise from the atrium bleeding into nearby Deck 3 cabins, though it usually quiets by late evening.
zones.mattersTo: Guests wanting total quiet in the evening should pick a cabin away from the atrium well; those who enjoy ambient music won't mind.

zones.what: Some aft Deck 6 balconies have a service ladder running from the roof of the Blu restaurant below (Deck 5) up past the veranda, and guests in that stretch heard banging/knocking noises from Blu until roughly 2-2:30am.
zones.effect: Intermittent late-night/early-morning mechanical or service noise from the restaurant below, on a ship the same reviewer otherwise described as unusually free of engine noise or vibration.
zones.mattersTo: Very light sleepers on the aft Deck 6 verandas above Blu should be aware; most guests found it a minor issue outweighed by an otherwise quiet ship.

zones.what: AquaClass cabins on Deck 11 sit directly beneath the fitness center on Deck 12.
zones.effect: A guest reported treadmill thumping every morning around 6am that crew could not resolve.
zones.mattersTo: Guests wanting to sleep past dawn should avoid AquaClass cabins stacked under the gym; early risers who exercise themselves won't mind.
zones.source: Cruise Critic boards thread "Avoid Aqua class cabins on deck 11"

zones.what: Deck 11 sits directly beneath the Deck 12 pool deck.
zones.effect: As with most ships, early-morning lounger movement and pool-deck foot traffic carry down into Deck 11 cabins.
zones.mattersTo: Guests hoping for a lie-in should avoid Deck 11; those planning to be up early for the pool won't be bothered.
zones.source: cruisecritic.com Celebrity Solstice Cabins & Suites editor review

zones.what: Solstice-class ships have a midship 'hump' where the hull steps outward; Solstice, as the lead ship, even carried a large glass 'X' logo on the hump-stateroom railings as part of the original design.
zones.effect: Cabins on the flat part of the hump (e.g. 6216-6234/6217-6235, 7266-7284/7221-7239, 8232-8250/8259-8277, 9272-9290/9217-9235) get an unobstructed straight-down view where straight-hull cabins nearby are blocked by lifeboats or structure, and several hump balconies run roughly three times the size of a standard veranda.
zones.mattersTo: Anyone wanting the biggest balcony and a clear view straight down (not just outward) should target these specific ranges; guests who don't care about looking straight down gain little extra from the hump besides square footage.
zones.source: en.wikipedia.org Solstice-class article + cruisedeckplans.com deck 6/7/8/9 notes + perthtravelers.com first-person Deck 9 hump review

zones.what: Solstice has only two elevator/stair banks - forward and midship (the midship bank is glass, rising through the atrium) - with no dedicated aft bank.
zones.effect: Reaching aft venues from Deck 11 upward requires walking aft and using stairs, or crossing an open weather deck on 12/14; cabins near the glass midship bank also sit close to the atrium, where live music and events are audible in the elevator lobby and can carry into nearby cabins.
zones.mattersTo: Guests who dislike long walks value the midship bank's convenience; those sensitive to atrium noise or wanting an aft-access shortcut should book away from it.
zones.source: Cruise Critic member review 218117 (elevator layout) + Fodor's Travel Talk forum thread on atrium noise near elevators

zones.what: Low, aft cabins are flagged for engine noise and vibration, while low, forward cabins can pick up bow-thruster noise during docking/undocking.
zones.effect: The effect is inconsistent across reports: some guides flag aft-lower cabins for vibration, while at least one detailed first-person Solstice review found the ship 'extremely quiet' with almost no transmitted engine noise or vibration in her cabin.
zones.mattersTo: Vibration-sensitive sleepers should still default to a mid, higher-up cabin as a precaution, but shouldn't assume aft-lower cabins will be loud on this particular ship.
zones.source: perthtravelers.com Solstice veranda review + Cruise Critic member review 553734 (counter-evidence of a quiet ship)

zones.what: A Solstice-specific cabin guide flags decks 3, 6, 11 and 12 as decks to 'be careful of,' and separately recommends a mid-ship, lower deck for guests prone to seasickness.
zones.effect: Far-forward cabins on the highest guest decks (11-12) will feel the most pitch and roll in rough seas; low, midship cabins feel the least motion.
zones.mattersTo: Motion-sensitive cruisers should avoid forward cabins on 11/12 and favor mid-ship, lower decks (7-9 per the same guide).
zones.source: perthtravelers.com Celebrity Solstice Veranda Stateroom Review

zones.what: Aft-facing balconies on decks 6 through 11 are cantilevered but are visible from the Sunset Bar and the outdoor buffet dining area located above them.
zones.effect: Guests on these aft balconies can be seen (and can see) diners/drinkers above, reducing privacy even though the balcony itself is not obstructed.
zones.mattersTo: Guests wanting private balcony time (sunbathing, etc.) should avoid this stack; those who don't mind being overlooked gain wake views instead.
zones.source: cruisecritic.com Celebrity Solstice Cabins & Suites editor review

zones.what: Many interior cabins on Solstice-class ships run lengthwise along the corridor with the entrance on the short wall, so the long wall (where the bed sits) faces the hallway rather than just the door.
zones.effect: Passersby end up walking alongside the bed wall rather than just past the entrance, which cruisers report as feeling 'more like a hallway than a cabin' and noisier from late-night hallway chatter.
zones.mattersTo: Light sleepers booking interior cabins should ask about the room's orientation; guests who don't mind hallway sound won't notice a difference from category alone.
zones.source: cruisegalore.com Best and Worst Celebrity Cabins guide

zones.what: Celebrity Solstice has 121 connecting rooms on board, including Veranda staterooms whose connecting pairs share adjoining balconies.
zones.effect: Families/groups can link two cabins with a connecting door and adjoining balconies for easier supervision of children, though connecting doors are reported anecdotally as a possible sound path between rooms.
zones.mattersTo: Families traveling together benefit; solo travelers or couples wanting full sound isolation from neighbors should ask for a non-connecting cabin.
zones.source: cruisecritic.com Celebrity Solstice Cabins & Suites editor review

zones.what: Service/crew access doors (laundry carts, room-service staging, internal stairwell access) are scattered along guest corridors on Solstice-class ships, generally unlabeled on deck plans as plain utility boxes.
zones.effect: Cabins next to these doors can pick up cart-rolling, door-banging and crew-conversation noise concentrated around turn-down and early-morning service hours; a Solstice-specific guest asked directly about reported crew-area noise near cabin 7320 but no confirmed public account was found.
zones.mattersTo: Very light sleepers should ask their travel agent or Celebrity to check for adjacent service doors before booking a specific cabin number.
zones.source: cruisesnooze.com Celebrity Silhouette cabins-to-avoid guide (same Solstice-class hull, service-door pattern generalized) + Cruise Critic boards thread on cabin 7320 (unconfirmed, Solstice-specific)

leads.claim: Reviewer states these balconies were 'worse than obstructed' - the deck extends ~10 feet past the rail and crew were frequently on that extended deck while in port.
leads.source: Cruise Critic member review, titled "Avoid Cabin 6301 & 6303"

leads.claim: Flagged on the ship's obstructed-view page as cabins with a lifeboat/structure view looking at the window or balcony.
leads.source: cruisedeckplans.com Celebrity Solstice Obstructed View page

leads.claim: The largest lifeboats on Deck 6 sit directly in front of this specific range, making the obstruction more severe than elsewhere on the deck.
Located below the nightclub on Deck 4; some noise reports from that venue.
Hump-section verandas on Deck 9 with balconies noticeably larger (extra depth not shown on the standard deck plan) than standard verandas.
leads.source: perthtravelers.com first-person Celebrity Solstice veranda review

leads.claim: Listed as the largest balconies on Deck 8, generally corresponding to the hump section.
A prospective guest asked specifically whether this cabin experiences crew-area noise; no confirmed firsthand answer was found in the thread at time of research.
leads.source: Cruise Critic boards thread "Crew noise by cabin 7320 on solstice?"

unknowns: Whether the highest guest decks (e.g. 15, or suites on 11/12) sit atop an inward hull taper that hides the straight-down view while keeping the horizon clear - no ship-specific source confirmed this for Solstice.
Exact hump cabin numbers on Deck 10 - source text was garbled/truncated and could not be confirmed with confidence.
Precise routing of the crew ('I-95')-style corridor on Solstice itself - only inferred from an identical-layout sister ship (Silhouette), not confirmed firsthand for Solstice.

Specific deck/cabin range affected by anchor-chain noise - one source lumped anchor noise in with 'low and at the rear' engine noise, which is inconsistent with typical bow anchor placement; not reliable enough to state as fact.

Whether Celebrity's official obstructed-view labeling (2C/2D) covers the full lifeboat-affected range on Decks 7-9, or only Deck 6 - sources only confirmed formal labeling for Deck 6 categories 2C/2D.
